thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Plaid (Software Engineering (SWE), entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Ownership-and-pragmatism bar: engineering leadership publicly prizes an overdeveloped sense of responsibility, honest discussion of real failures, and business-problem pragmatism over perfect systems. No pass rate is published in fetched sources. Note: 1 fact(s) in this record are past their freshness window and flagged stale — re-verify before acting on them.

- Plaid's stated principles in job materials include impact and growing together (HEART: hum — reported pattern, not a measured share: Plaid's stated principles in job materials include impact and growing together (HEART: humility, energy, ambition, resilience, teamwork), per a posting summary indexed from Plaid materials. (source: https://plaid.com/careers/openings/engineering/san-francisco-hq/staff-software-engineer-ai-applications/, as of 2026-10-12)
Known biases of this data: Survivorship bias: the apprentice blog post is a success story published by the employer; it cannot show apprentice acceptance rates or failure modes.; Single-story risk: one documented path is evidence a route exists, not that it is common.; Leadership-interview statements are one executive's described preferences, not audited hiring data.; Glassdoor-style reports are self-selected and unverified; used only as labeled anecdotes.; No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).
